You are working in the Ligra graph-processing framework at /workspace.
The framework (/workspace/ligra/*.h) is COMPLETE and already implements
vertexSubset, edgeMap/edgeMapData/edgeMapDense/edgeMapDenseForward/edgeMapSparse/
edgeMapSparse_no_filter, edgeMapFilter, packEdges, vertexMap, vertexFilter,
vertexFilter2 and parallel_main. DO NOT MODIFY ANY FILE under /workspace/ligra/,
and DO NOT MODIFY /workspace/apps/Makefile or any other app's .C file.
Your ONLY writable file is the single .C file named in your task.

Build & run (apps/ has symlinks to ../ligra/*.h already):
  cd /workspace/apps && make <AppName>
Compiler line: g++ -std=c++14 -O3 -DBYTERLE -o <App> <App>.C

CRITICAL framework facts (verify by reading the headers before coding):
* In the default build, parallel.h maps parallel_for -> plain `for` (single
  threaded). Code must still be written with correct atomics (CAS/writeMin/
  writeAdd) as upstream Ligra does, but execution is deterministic.
* Types: uintE/intE (32-bit by default), uintT/intT, UINT_E_MAX, INT_E_MAX.
* ligra/utils.h provides: CAS, writeMin, writeAdd, hashInt, newA, granular_for,
  sequence::plusReduce, sequence::plusScan, pbbs::* . There is NO writeOr --
  if you need atomic bitwise-or, define it locally in your .C file.
* edgeMap signature:
    edgeMap(graph<vertex>& GA, VS& vs, F f, intT threshold = -1, const flags& fl = 0)
  flags available: no_output, pack_edges, sparse_no_filter, dense_forward,
  dense_parallel, remove_duplicates, no_dense, edge_parallel.
  threshold -1 means "use GA.m/20".
* The user struct F passed to edgeMap must provide update(s,d),
  updateAtomic(s,d) and cond(d). For WEIGHTED apps the signatures are
  update(s,d,weight) / updateAtomic(s,d,weight).
* vertexMap(VS& V, F f) calls f(v) for a plain vertexSubset.
* vertexFilter(vertexSubset V, F filter) -> dense-based result.
  vertexFilter2(...) -> sparse-based result.
* vertexSubset constructors: vertexSubset(n) empty; vertexSubset(n, v) single
  vertex; vertexSubset(n, m, uintE* sparseArray); vertexSubset(n, m, bool* dense).
  Methods: isEmpty(), numNonzeros(), numRows(), toSparse(), toDense(), del(),
  vtx(i), isIn(v), dense().
* cond_true(d) is provided for "always true" cond functions.
* Every app is a template function:
    template <class vertex> void Compute(graph<vertex>& GA, commandLine P) {...}
  It MUST be a template over vertex, because parallel_main instantiates it for
  symmetricVertex, asymmetricVertex, compressedSymmetricVertex and
  compressedAsymmetricVertex. Therefore ONLY use the vertex methods that also
  exist on compressed vertices: getOutDegree(), getInDegree(),
  decodeOutNgh / decodeInNghBreakEarly / decodeOutNghSparse /
  decodeOutNghSparseSeq / countOutNgh / packOutNgh / copyOutNgh.
  *** DO NOT call getOutNeighbor(j) / getOutNeighbors() / getInNeighbor(j) in an
  app *** -- those do not exist on compressed vertices and the app must keep
  compiling once Ligra+ compressed vertices are implemented. If you need the
  neighbour list, materialize it with copyOutNgh (see apps/Triangle.C for the
  exact idiom) or use countOutNgh with a predicate.
* Read /workspace/apps/BFS.C, /workspace/apps/PageRank.C and
  /workspace/apps/Triangle.C first -- match their style, comment density and
  the 23-line MIT licence header they carry.
* /workspace/tutorial/*.C contains SKELETONS with "//FILL IN" markers showing
  the intended structure of some apps. Use them as structural hints only.

Inputs: ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (symmetric, unweighted, n=128 m=708,
run with -s) and ../inputs/rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 (symmetric, WEIGHTED, run with -s).

Always finish by actually building and running your app and confirming the
output is sane. Report exactly what you ran and what it printed.


You are an INDEPENDENT VERIFIER for /workspace/apps/KCore.C, which another agent just wrote.

The spec it was given was:
Implement /workspace/apps/KCore.C -- k-core decomposition (peeling) on a
symmetric graph. /workspace/tutorial/KCore.C shows the exact intended structure
(with //FILL IN holes) -- follow it but use the framework types.
* intE* Degrees initialized to GA.V[i].getOutDegree(); uintE* coreNumbers.
* Deg_LessThan_K<vertex>: operator()(i) returns true when Degrees[i] < k, and
  in that case records coreNumbers[i] = k-1 and zeroes Degrees[i].
* Deg_AtLeast_K<vertex>: operator()(i) returns Degrees[i] >= k.
* Update_Deg: update/updateAtomic decrement Degrees[d] (updateAtomic uses
  writeAdd(&Degrees[d],-1)); cond(d) returns Degrees[d] > 0.
* Compute: frontier starts as all n vertices. For k = 1..n: repeatedly
  vertexFilter the frontier into toRemove (Deg_LessThan_K) and remaining
  (Deg_AtLeast_K); if toRemove is empty this k is a fixed point, break; else
  edgeMap from toRemove with Update_Deg to decrement neighbour degrees.
  When the frontier becomes empty, largestCore = k-1 and stop.
* Report "largestCore was <N>" and also "KCore max core: <N>".
* Sanity-check the answer yourself: the largest core number of this graph can
  be computed independently with a short python peeling script over
  ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 -- do that and confirm the two agree. Report both.
* Run: ./KCore -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100

Its report was:
**FILE:** `/workspace/apps/KCore.C` (new, 126 lines; MIT header matching BFS.C/PageRank.C/Triangle.C). No other file touched — `apps/Makefile` and `ligra/ligra.h` were already modified in the starting snapshot, and `git diff` confirms I added nothing to them.

**IMPLEMENTATION** — follows `/workspace/tutorial/KCore.C` structure with framework types (`intE* Degrees`, `uintE* coreNumbers`, `uintE` functor args instead of the tutorial's `long*`/`long`):
- `Update_Deg`: `update` does `Degrees[d]--`, `updateAtomic` does `writeAdd(&Degrees[d],(intE)-1)` (the `(intE)` cast is required — `writeAdd` is `template<class ET> void writeAdd(ET*, ET)`, so a bare `-1` breaks deduction under `-DEDGELONG` where `intE` is `long`), `cond(d)` is `Degrees[d] > 0`.
- `Deg_LessThan_K` / `Deg_AtLeast_K` templated on `vertex`; the former records `coreNumbers[i]=k-1` and zeroes `Degrees[i]`.
- `Compute`: frontier = all n; per k, `vertexFilter` into `toRemove` then `remaining`, break on empty `toRemove`, else `edgeMap(GA,toRemove,Update_Deg(Degrees),-1,no_output)`.
- Only compressed-safe vertex methods used (`getOutDegree()`); all decoding goes through `edgeMap`, so this stays compilable once Ligra+ vertices land.

**COMMANDS AND OUTPUT**

```
cd /workspace/apps && make KCore
g++ -std=c++14 -O3   -DBYTERLE   -o KCore KCore.C
```
(clean, zero warnings/errors)

```
cd /workspace/apps && ./KCore -s -rounds 1 ../inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100
largestCore was 4
KCore max core: 4
largestCore was 4
KCore max core: 4
Running time : 3e-05
```

**INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION** — three ways, all agree on **4**:
1. Python peeling mirroring the app's loop structure: `largestCore = 4`, core histogram `{0:3, 1:5, 2:25, 3:38, 4:57}`.
2. Python classic smallest-last degeneracy ordering (structurally different algorithm): `degeneracy = 4`.
3. Stronger check — I compiled a debug copy **outside** `apps/` (`g++ ... -I/workspace/apps -o /tmp/KCoreDbg /tmp/KCoreDbg.C`, `apps/KCore.C` unmodified) that dumps all 128 per-vertex core numbers, and `diff`ed against the degeneracy-ordering result: **identical for all 128 vertices**, not just the max. Temp files deleted afterward.

Input sanity: n=128, m=708, 0 asymmetric pairs, 0 self-loops, 0 duplicate adjacency entries — so the "assumes symmetric" precondition genuinely holds and the induced-degree bookkeeping cannot be skewed by self-loops.

**CONCERNS** (none blocking)
- The output appears twice. This is `parallel_main` in `ligra/ligra.h:530-535`: one untimed warm-up `Compute` plus `rounds` timed ones, so `-rounds 1` gives 2 invocations. `./BFS -s -rounds 1` double-prints identically, confirming it is framework behavior, not app state leakage. `-rounds 3` produced 4 identical results, so `Compute` is idempotent (all state is local and freed).
- Break-early interaction is intentional, not a bug: `edgeMapDense` calls `decodeInNghBreakEarly`, which stops scanning a vertex once `cond(d)` goes false. Since `cond` is `Degrees[d] > 0` and `Deg_LessThan_K` zeroes degrees on removal, degrees can never go negative and already-peeled vertices are never decremented again — dropped decrements are provably irrelevant because such a vertex is already removed at this k.
- `no_output` avoids allocating a result frontier; it also sidesteps the duplicate vertices the sparse path would otherwise emit. Behavior is unchanged if you swap in the tutorial's `vertexSubset output = edgeMap(...)` form.
- Not exercised: the weighted input (`Update_Deg` has unweighted `update(s,d)` signatures, correct for this unweighted-build app) and the `-c` compressed path (`compressedVertex.h` is still a stub in this workspace — task #4).

Your job: try to REFUTE that this app is correct and complete.
1. Read the file. Check it really implements the named algorithm (not a stub or a
   trivially-wrong shortcut), that it is `template <class vertex>`, and that it
   does NOT call getOutNeighbor/getOutNeighbors/getInNeighbor/getInNeighbors
   (those break on compressed vertices later).
2. Rebuild from scratch: cd /workspace/apps && rm -f KCore && make KCore
   -- it must compile with no errors. Warnings are acceptable.
3. Run it and check the printed numbers are actually right. Where feasible,
   compute the ground truth INDEPENDENTLY with a small python script over
   /workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100 (or rMatGraph_WJ_5_100 for the weighted
   app) and compare. Do not trust the implementation's own claims.
4. Confirm it does not modify anything under /workspace/ligra/, the Makefile,
   or another app (check: cd /workspace && git status --short).

If you find a real defect, FIX IT in KCore.C (that file only), rebuild,
rerun, and re-verify. Then report.

Return: VERDICT (PASS or FIXED or BROKEN), the ground-truth values you computed
independently, the values the app printed, and anything still wrong.

cat > /tmp/gt_kcore.py <<'EOF'
import sys
p='/workspace/inputs/rMatGraph_J_5_100'
tok=open(p).read().split()
assert tok[0]=='AdjacencyGraph'
n=int(tok[1]); m=int(tok[2])
off=[int(x) for x in tok[3:3+n]]
edges=[int(x) for x in tok[3+n:3+n+m]]
assert len(edges)==m, (len(edges),m)
adj=[]
for i in range(n):
    s=off[i]; e=off[i+1] if i+1<n else m
    adj.append(edges[s:e])
print("n",n,"m",m)
# structural sanity, computed here independently
selfloops=sum(1 for i in range(n) for j in adj[i] if j==i)
dups=sum(len(a)-len(set(a)) for a in adj)
S=set((i,j) for i in range(n) for j in adj[i])
asym=sum(1 for (i,j) in S if (j,i) not in S)
print("selfloops",selfloops,"dup_entries",dups,"asym_pairs",asym)
print("degsum",sum(len(a) for a in adj))

# --- Method A: peeling exactly mirroring the app (degree = adjacency length) ---
deg=[len(adj[i]) for i in range(n)]
alive=[True]*n
core=[0]*n
remaining=n
largest=-1
for k in range(1,n+1):
    while True:
        toRemove=[i for i in range(n) if alive[i] and deg[i]<k]
        if not toRemove:
            break
        for i in toRemove:
            core[i]=k-1; deg[i]=0; alive[i]=False
        for i in toRemove:
            for j in adj[i]:
                if alive[j]:
                    deg[j]-=1
    if not any(alive):
        largest=k-1
        break
print("METHOD_A largestCore =",largest)
hist={}
for c in core: hist[c]=hist.get(c,0)+1
print("METHOD_A core histogram",dict(sorted(hist.items())))

# --- Method B: classic smallest-last / bucket degeneracy ordering (different algorithm) ---
import heapq
deg2=[len(adj[i]) for i in range(n)]
removed=[False]*n
h=[(deg2[i],i) for i in range(n)]
heapq.heapify(h)
core2=[0]*n
best=0
while h:
    d,v=heapq.heappop(h)
    if removed[v] or d!=deg2[v]: continue
    removed[v]=True
    best=max(best,deg2[v])
    core2[v]=best
    for u in adj[v]:
        if not removed[u]:
            deg2[u]-=1
            heapq.heappush(h,(deg2[u],u))
print("METHOD_B degeneracy =",max(core2))
print("METHOD_B agrees per-vertex with A:",core2==core)
if core2!=core:
    diffs=[(i,core[i],core2[i]) for i in range(n) if core[i]!=core2[i]]
    print("first diffs",diffs[:10],"count",len(diffs))
open('/tmp/gt_cores.txt','w').write("\n".join("%d %d"%(i,core2[i]) for i in range(n))+"\n")
EOF

import random, os

    for i in range(n):
        for j in adj[i]:
            if i!=j: S[i].add(j); S[j].add(i)
    adj=[sorted(s) for s in S]

        d,v=heapq.heappop(h)
        if removed[v] or d!=deg[v]: continue
        removed[v]=True; best=max(best,deg[v]); core[v]=best
        for u in adj[v]:
            if not removed[u]:
                deg[u]-=1; heapq.heappush(h,(deg[u],u))
    return core

for name,(n,m,adj) in tests.items():
    core=degeneracy(n,adj)
    open(name+'.cores','w').write("\n".join("%d %d"%(i,core[i]) for i in range(n))+"\n")
    print(name, "n=%d m=%d"%(n,m), "degeneracy=", max(core))
EOF

for g in g_rand g_mix g_path g_hub; do

  got=$(grep -m1 largestCore /tmp/$g.appout)

  # take only the first n CORE lines (first of the 2 runs)
  nv=$(wc -l < /tmp/$g.cores)
  grep "^CORE " /tmp/$g.appout | head -$nv | awk '{print $2" "$3}' > /tmp/$g.appcores
  if diff -q /tmp/$g.appcores /tmp/$g.cores >/dev/null; then st="cores MATCH ($nv vertices)"; else st="cores MISMATCH: $(diff /tmp/$g.appcores /tmp/$g.cores | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"; fi
  echo "$g: $got | $st"
done
